query: For an equimolar WTaTiVZr high-entropy alloy made from low-activation refractory elements, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains its plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading relevant to sustained plasma-facing-component service? Specify a controlled comparison that would isolate the hypothesized cause, the observations expected relative to pure tungsten, the applicable boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The high configurational entropy in the equimolar WTaTiVZr high-entropy alloy leads to the formation of a solid-solution phase, which enhances its plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
generation.conditions: High-temperature mechanical loading relevant to sustained plasma-facing-component service
generation.mechanism: High configurational entropy favoring the formation of a solid-solution phase
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten
generation.boundary: High-temperature mechanical loading relevant to sustained plasma-facing-component service
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between the high configurational entropy and the formation of a solid-solution phase, and its impact on the plastic strain and toughness of the alloy

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled comparison of the plastic strain and toughness of the equimolar WTaTiVZr high-entropy alloy and commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the plastic strain and toughness of the equimolar WTaTiVZr high-entropy alloy are not significantly higher than those of commercially used pure tungsten, then the hypothesis is falsified

As a new class of metallic materials, HEAs or complicated concentrated alloys made up of four or more primary elements greatly increase the alloy design space [,,]. HEA microstructures can be tailored to suit desired qualities, including single-phase solid solution HEAs [,,] and HEAs with hierarchical microstructures [,,,]. Moreover, over a wide temperature range, an increasing number of appealing features in HEAs have been revealed, including an outstanding strength–ductility synergy at ambient temperature [,], extraordinary mechanical capabilities at cryogenic temperatures [], and ultrahigh strength at extreme temperatures [].
Refractory HEAs (RHEAs) stand out among various types of HEAs due to their unparalleled mechanical properties at high temperatures exceeding 800 °C, and even up to 1500 °C in some cases [,], making them viable options for high-temperature structural applications, outperforming typical Ni-based superalloys. ## 2. Materials and Methods
The as-cast metal ingots were prepared by vacuum arc melting; all the used raw material elements had a high purity (>99.9 atomic percent, at%). Prior to arc-melting the raw materials, the residual oxygen in the arc-melter chamber was absorbed using a high-purity Ti-getter. The chemical composition of the metal ingots was NbTaHfTiZrV0.5. All ingots were flipped over and remelted more than 5–8 times to promote the homogeneity. The specific composition of the alloy is shown in Table 1. The weight of as-cast samples was 30 g. The ingots were then drop-cast into a copper mold that was water-cooled and had dimensions of 36 × 12 × 3 mm. The XRD equipment model was the Aeris (PANalytical B.V., Alemlo, The Netherlands). Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were used to analyze the microstructure of RHEA samples in diverse experimental scenarios. To be specific, we used a scanning electron microscope (SEM) equipped with a backscatter electron (BSE) mode to investigate the microstructures and structural evolution. The content of elements in each sample was further studied by energy dispersion spectroscopy (EDS). The SEM and EDS tests used the same equipment, the model was a PhenomWorld (Phenom, Eindhoven, The Netherlands).
